overview: Zambia's femtech ecosystem is anchored by Dawa Health, whose AI-enabled DawaMom platform for maternal, postnatal and cervical cancer prevention care grew out of the Lusaka accelerator BongoHive and in 2025 was selected for UNICEF Femtech Ventures. Alongside it sits a strong civil-society layer led by Copper Rose Zambia on menstrual health and SRHR, plus government commitments on reproductive health commodities, free sanitary pads in schools, and nationwide HPV screening. The market is thin on venture capital but supported by gender-lens funds active across Southern Africa and by donor-backed accelerator grants.

sections.heading: Latest major news
sections.narrative: Recent activity clusters around Dawa Health's international recognition and expanding women's health programs.

items.text: DawaMom by Dawa Health (Zambia) named among 11 startups in the first UNICEF Femtech Ventures cohort, from 1,100+ applications across 85 countries.
BongoHive's Women in Tech Zambia accelerator (with a HealthTech focus area) ran its cohort, awarding USD 10,000 equity-free grants to five women-led startups.
Zambia's Ministry of Education received sanitary pads and school books to support the free sanitary pad policy for female learners.
Preliminary 2024 Zambia Demographic and Health Survey results released, covering contraceptive use, maternal health and gender-based violence.
Dawa Health's use of AI to analyze ultrasound scans and flag high-risk pregnancies in Zambia profiled by Forbes.

sections.heading: Policy & strategy
sections.narrative: National strategy links digital health, reproductive health financing and menstrual equity.

items.text: Zambia's Digital Health Strategy 2022-2026 prioritizes electronic health records, telemedicine and data analytics toward Universal Health Coverage.
Government signed a Compact of Commitment with UNFPA to boost domestic funding for family planning and maternal health supplies, since disbursing over USD 11.4M.
HPV vaccination moved to a routine single-dose schedule as Zambia scales cervical cancer prevention toward WHO 2030 elimination targets.
Government free sanitary pad policy for public schools advanced, with pads supplied and improved female sanitation facilities to keep girls in class.

sections.heading: Latest ecosystem moves
sections.narrative: Accelerators, donor programs and NGOs form the backbone of women's health innovation.

items.text: Dawa Health originated at BongoHive, the Lusaka startup accelerator, and now runs DawaMom via web, mobile, SMS and multilingual chatbot with community health workers.
BongoHive's Women in Tech Zambia accelerator supports women-led tech businesses with a dedicated HealthTech challenge and equity-free grants.
Copper Rose Zambia runs grassroots menstrual health and SRHR programs, having educated over 5,000 adolescents through its Candid Pride and Woman4Her campaigns.
UNFPA Zambia, with the Ministry of Health and Lifeline/Childline, distributes sanitary pads via mobile health clinics across Eastern, Southern and Western Provinces.
World Vision Zambia distributed menstrual hygiene management packs to 750 girls across 16 schools in Manyinga and Mufumbwe districts.
